reviewer.independence: Separate from implementation agent. Review was not blind. No product-source edit, commit, external post, or approval transition. Only this report was authored.

scope.limit: ONE bounded design-only refinement of the preferred candidate; not a visual restart, production implementation, final Design System approval or owner acceptance.

verdict: PASS FOR PRODUCT OWNER VISUAL REVIEW
verdictBoundary: Independent visual judgment based on actual browser images and bounded interaction checks. Final technical QA/CI and final screenshot artifact binding are reported separately; neither this verdict nor CI can grant owner visual/content acceptance.

actualEnvironment.method: Actual browser renders. Narrow/tablet screenshots full-page;1440px desktop screenshot is1200px viewport. No generated-image mockups.

visualCritique.criterion: Patient reading length and repeated navigation
visualCritique.judgment: Material improvement. The page now has one compact retrieval section instead of repeated summary/history discovery and a second Find care CTA. The single global Find care remains unmistakably interactive. All five secondary destinations remain: summaries/follow-up, appointments, prescriptions, available history, and doctors. The shared-summary empty state and care-permission meaning remain explicit. Appointment date, complete doctor name, clinic, localized12h time and primary detail CTA still dominate.

Material improvement. Source context opens immediately before the editor in normal flow, with exact patient, named Gregorian date,24h range, IANA zone/offset and current independent care authority, then source-specific states. Allergy uncertainty is visible even while collapsed. Return closes the panel and restores focus to its opener at about24px from the viewport top, without a page-tail jump or sticky masking.

visualCritique.criterion: Doctor task access and sustained work
visualCritique.judgment: Three local task links are directly visible. Documentation, Follow-up and Review & close focus their own in-place panels; they remain separate from global Schedule/People in your care. Unsaved textarea content survived a Documentation→Follow-up→Review & close→Documentation round trip in independent tests. Source context remains available for each task. No automatic save/sign/release/close behavior was observed.

The composition is more decisive and less repetitive: date-led appointment, a clearly prioritized full-width narrow CTA, compact flat retrieval rows and a connected professional writing plane. Violet keylines and differentiated shapes support hierarchy without introducing a palette restart, glow, decorative gradients, metrics or equal-sized dashboard tiles. This reads as a product refinement rather than a component test wall. Personality remains deliberately restrained and familiar rather than highly expressive or unusually original.

Dark remains dark across canvas, raised context and editor, with controlled lavender actions and no white slabs. Light uses the same task hierarchy with airy canvas and a distinct writing surface. Patient and Doctor remain visibly related but differ appropriately in density and task continuity. No theme default/system/persistence policy was introduced.

Arabic is composed as a primary layout, with complete names and natural labels; professional time and IANA identifiers preserve order. English task labels fit through content-driven wrapping. Independently checked Doctor AR/EN320px at200% text: no document overflow; local tasks expand to comfortable full-width rows. The final decorative account avatar grows with text to contain its initials. Tablet and desktop retain the same selected visual language.

No observed semantic regression in this static preview: booking remains independent from care authority, private note does not become patient-visible, summary and follow-up remain separate unreleased sources, and close retains explicit irreversible/no-save/no-sign/no-release consequences. No fabricated summary/history/clinical finding or Lab/AI capability was added. These observations do not test real backend authority or clinical transactions.

measurementInterpretation: 390×1200 CSS viewport,100% text, Light, DPR1. Patient AR1974→1296px and EN2081→1338px; duplicate Find care links2→1. Doctor initial Documentation AR3088→1964px and EN3230→2077px; direct visible local tasks0→3. Heights are structural observations, not measured cognitive effort, participant usability or a quality score. findingsResolved.finding: Near-editor disclosure initially contained source states without exact patient/visit/authority identity.
findingsResolved.resolution: Added compact patient, full dated24h visit, IANA offset and current/separate-booking authority within the disclosure; independently rechecked in Documentation and Follow-up.

findingsResolved.finding: At200% text the fixed40px account avatar visually overfilled with32px initials.
findingsResolved.resolution: Narrow avatar dimensions now use2.5rem:40px at100%,80px at200%. Independent current-browser200% render visually contains the initials and normal390px renders remain byte-identical.

remainingTradeoffs: Doctor first editor begins slightly lower after explicit task/context controls: AR about702→740px; EN about776→818px. Do not claim faster first-field entry. The gain is task discovery and local recovery of source context rather than reduced first-fold height.

Expanded source context is tall because truthful identity, authority and independent source states remain readable. It opens in place and closes predictably; it does not stay permanently beside mobile authoring.
The Patient secondary list and permission explanation still require some scrolling. Reducing repetition does not establish physical-device or participant usability.
The visual expression remains conservative. Final premium/aesthetic preference belongs to the Product Owner.
